issues.description: Method name/signature mismatch for the farm song: the problem statement and template define a public method singFarmSong(), but the reference solution implements it as playFarmSong() instead. This inconsistency in the public API (method name) can confuse students about which method to implement or call and may break tests or example code that expect singFarmSong().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution use the same public method name as specified in the problem and template: rename playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() method that delegates to the existing playFarmSong() implementation. Ensure the method signature and visibility match the problem statement and template.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Farm method named singFarmSong(), but the solution implements this public behavior under the different name playFarmSong(). This diverging identifier for the same conceptual action (playing/singing the farm song) creates a direct mapping confusion: students following the specification or the template will look for singFarmSong(), while the reference solution exposes playFarmSong(), which may prevent straightforward comparison, cause uncommented Main examples to not compile, and increase extraneous cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's public method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong() (or add a singFarmSong() wrapper that delegates to playFarmSong()) so the solution, template, and problem statement use the same identifier for the farm-song behavior.
